chunks: And Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother (peace be upon him), from a man who spent the night in Mecca during the nights of Mina until morning,
he said: 'If he visited it during the day and spent the night in it until morning, then upon him is blood (of a sacrificial animal) that he must shed.'

key_terms.دَمٌ: Blood, referring to the sacrificial animal (qurbani) required as a ritual offering
key_terms.مِنًى: Mina, a valley near Mecca where pilgrims stay during Hajj
key_terms.يُهَرِيقُهُ: He must shed/slaughter, referring to the act of sacrificing the animal

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who spends the night in Mina after visiting it during the day?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq clarifies the legal distinction between the obligatory stay (wuquf) in Mina during the day and the voluntary overnight stay, imposing a sacrificial animal (dam) as a penalty for the latter. In Shia jurisprudence, this highlights the precision required in replicating the Prophet's and Imams' practices during Hajj, where deviations from the prescribed ritual timing incur specific expiations. The ruling underscores the importance of adhering strictly to the temporal boundaries of Hajj rituals to ensure the validity of the pilgrimage.
